observations: Indoor and outdoor units of a split-system air conditioner are shown together on a tiled floor.
The word 'inverter' is printed on the front of the outdoor unit in photo 0.
There is red marker writing on the outdoor unit that appears to say '44,000' in photo 0.
The units show signs of use, including dust and minor scuffs.
No manufacturer nameplate or technical specification sticker is visible on the sides of the units.
A logo is visible on the top right of the indoor unit but the text is not legible.

claims.evidence: The seller later states 'No fault at all' in the same description.
The seller opens the description stating 'Faulty inverter AC'.

claims.claim: Barely used, bought new last year
claims.evidence: The red marker price '44,000' on the casing is typical of second-hand or scrap yard inventory, not a domestic 'bought new' history.
These documents are mentioned but not pictured.

risks.proof: A clear photo of the silver nameplate sticker on the side of the indoor or outdoor unit.
A video of the unit powered on, showing the indoor unit display and the outdoor fan spinning.
A photo showing the remote control and the copper connecting pipes.

proof_requests: Photo of the nameplate/specification sticker on the side of the units to confirm HP and model.
Photo of the receipt and warranty card mentioned.
Video of the unit powered on and running.
Photos of the remote control and copper piping.
response.reason: The seller's description is self-contradictory regarding the condition ('Faulty' vs 'No fault'). Additionally, the cooling capacity (HP), which is the primary price driver, cannot be determined from the photos.
